newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's MATAV looks at share sale, interest high.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's MATAV looks at share sale, interest high.

text.p: Hungarian telecommunications company MATAV is considering an international share offering but the company's chief financial officer said on Friday no final decisions had been made.
"We at the company are looking at the possibility of doing an IPO in the future," said Ray Stewart, chief financial officer of MATAV.

The Financial Times in London reported earlier that Deutsche Telekom and Ameritech, which together own 67 percent of MATAV, would sell a 16 percent stake, worth about $500 million, within the next 18 months.
Stewart said the company had been talking to several investment banks but it was premature to discuss the size or timing of an offer.
"Nothing's been decided, whether there will be an IPO, or when the IPO will be -- if there is one -- or the size," he told Reuters.
Geza Laszlo, chief economist of MATAV financial subsidiary Investel, said earlier that the majority owners were planning to sell part of their holding but declined to say how much.
"We have a very interesting plan and it will be a major IPO in the region," Laszlo said.
Analysts said investors would take a keen interest in MATAV since Hungary's economy shows signs of strengthening with lower inflation and slightly higher GDP growth expected.
"I think people have been really waiting for an international listing for Matav for quite a long time," said John Oates, director of central and eastern European equities for UBS in London.

"Quite a few international institutions have bought in from local authorities. It is a stock that is followed in London and I think most people understand there is a good opportunity...and are going to take a very serious look at it."
"I think that based on the company's fundamentals, the offering could be very very successful," added Gabor Sitanyi of ING Barings in London.
"If inflation's downward trend continues and GDP growth picks up then the last barriers are basically over."

MATAV shares, which are traded on the OTC market in Budapest, have risen from 200 forints during the summer to 300 forints and could go as high as 450 forints with the IPO, said Laszlo Batora, analyst at Raffeisen Securities in Budapest.
"It was quite a good increase and I think the shares should generate interest, but the liquidity is low right now," Batora added.

Investel economist Laszlo said four investment banks have been chosen to formulate plans for the sale, with a deadline of November 15 to submit proposals. They are CS First Boston, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Merrill Lynch and Morgan Stanley.
He said there was no implication that Deutsche Telekom and Ameritech were losing confidence in MATAV, which holds a monopoly on land-based telecommunications in Hungary through the year 2001.

"I can tell you that we have now an interesting growth story in our portfolio," Laszlo said. "So if they want to go to the market probably it is a reasonable time because they can sell a good growth story."
"They want to see what the market says about the price," Laszlo said. "They want to show that their investment was reasonable."
Deutsche Telekom and Ameritech together bought 30 percent of Matav in 1993 for 850 million and purchased another 37 percent of the company in late 1995 for 852 million.

The Hungarian government holds a 25 percent stake with the remainder held by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, the International Finance Corporation, local governments and individual investors
